text:
jordan: FYI I noticed the console p99 for POST /v1/generate balloons when I slice by customer_tier=enterprise. p50/p95 basically unchanged. anyone have a checklist for when a p99 looks "wrong" vs real?

casey: common checklist: sample_count for the slice, whether rollup mode changed, any tag that could carry a tail (route, variant, throttle_reason), and if we mixed raw vs rolled data.

rahul: which panel is this? the new latency panel or the legacy view?

jordan: new panel. snapshot: global p50=95ms p95=220ms p99=760ms; enterprise slice p50=96ms p95=225ms p99=2.9s. sample_count in that minute ~3.7k.

metrics-bot: rollup modes (current): tdigest if samples >= 8k; histogram if 500 <= samples < 8k; raw-sample otherwise. (telemetry/rollups.md)

casey: histogram for 3.7k. our histograms for this endpoint set use 80ms buckets. a few multi-second outliers will end up congesting the top bucket.

lina: any idea where the outliers are coming from? routing fallback? throttling? model variant mismatch?

jordan: I grouped by routing_policy and model_variant. Quick query I ran:
```
SELECT minute, routing_policy, model_variant, count(*) as n, pctl(0.99, latency_ms) as p99
FROM requests
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND customer_tier='enterprise'
GROUP BY minute, routing_policy, model_variant
ORDER BY minute DESC
LIMIT 30;
```

rahul: results?

jordan: spikes correlate with routing_policy='fallback_to_cheap' and model_variant='qs8'. Those rows are ~0.6% of the slice but latencies 1.4s-3.2s.

casey: so a tiny origin dominates p99 because histogram buckets are coarse. Two UX changes we should do: 1) show a "percentile confidence" indicator that considers sample_count and top-origin concentration; 2) surface top contributing tag inline (e.g., "top contributor: routing_policy=fallback_to_cheap (0.6%)").

lina: the confidence indicator could be a simple three-state: high, medium, low. Rules: high if provenance=tdigest; medium if histogram and top-origin <=0.5%; low if histogram and top-origin >0.5% or sample_count < 2k; raw-sample always low. Thoughts?

rahul: I like it. Also propose an "interpolated pctl" fallback: when in histogram mode and top-origin is small but dominating tail, compute p99 as a weighted merge of per-origin p99s (compute p99 per tag from raw samples or tdigest where available, then weight by origin counts). That prevents a single outlier origin from dominating due to coarse buckets.

casey: we should also add a quick action on the panel: "break down by routing_policy" when confidence=low so an on-call can click and see the distribution. Low-effort UX: show sample_count and provenance badge (tdigest/histogram/raw) next to the metric.

jordan: can we compute confidence cheaply at query time?

metrics-bot: suggested metric for confidence calc: sample_count (n), proportion_in_top_bucket (p_top), unique_origin_count (u). Example rule: if provenance=histogram and (p_top > 0.5% OR n < 2000) => confidence=low. (internal doc ref: telemetry/confidence.md)

rahul: implementation plan: 
- short: show provenance badge + sample_count + top-3 contributor tags + confidence flag.
- medium: add "interpolated pctl" that computes per-tag p99 then blends. Make it optional behind a feature flag.
- long: change rollup policy to prefer tdigest for slices with mixed origins for pctl computation (more CPU) or compute pctl via sampled tdigest merge.

lina: also add an API param for the console to request p99_by_origin so the UI can fetch the per-origin p99s for the slice. That makes the breakdown fast without changing core rollups.

casey: agree. Example internal API: `GET /api/metrics/percentile?endpoint=/v1/generate&slice=customer_tier:enterprise&by=route,model_variant`. Returns counts + pctl per group.

jordan: I'll file CONSOLE-5010 with repro, the grouped SQL, and a suggested mockup showing confidence + top contributor. Tagging @casey @rahul @lina.

rahul: one more note: for alarms/SLOs we should default to a conservative p99 that excludes non-critical routing fallbacks unless explicitly included. Otherwise alerts will be noisy.

lina: good point. I'll open a separate RFC about SLO metric scoping.

jordan: thanks all. I'll attach the raw histogram bucket dump to the ticket so infra can see the top-bucket mass. closing for now :ok_hand:
